issues.legal_issue: A forgery-related FIR should be quashed where the authenticity of the documents is pending determination in a civil suit and the FIR rests on a handwriting expert’s opinion.
material_facts: A civil recovery suit was pending in which the authenticity of four receipts was directly in issue.

A handwriting expert opined that the signatures on the receipts did not match the purported signer’s signatures, but the opinion was not conclusive and could be challenged by evidence or assessed by the court comparing writings.
The FIR alleging forgery and related offences was registered after the expert’s opinion, while the civil court had not yet determined whether the receipts were genuine.
issues.conclusion: The FIR should not continue while the authenticity of the receipts is pending in the civil suit; its continuation would prejudice the parties and amount to an abuse of process. The FIR was quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 45 of the Indian Evidence Act, a handwriting expert’s opinion is relevant but not conclusive evidence. Section 73 empowers the court to compare admitted and disputed writings. Where the genuineness of documents is pending in a civil suit, an FIR based on the expert opinion alone should not continue; the Court exercised its power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to quash it. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.petition_to_quash_forgery_fir: A person accused in a forgery-related FIR seeks to have that FIR quashed.
predicates.civil_suit_pending_on_document_authentic: A civil suit is pending in which the authenticity of the same documents is directly in issue.
predicates.expert_report_was_only_basis_for_fir: The FIR was registered on the basis of a handwriting expert’s opinion that the disputed signatures were not made by the purported signer.

issues.definition: When a person seeks to quash a forgery-related FIR, a civil suit is already considering the authenticity of the same documents, and the FIR rests only on a handwriting expert’s opinion, the FIR is quashed as an abuse of process.

issues.legal_issue: A cheque-dishonour complaint should not be quashed on disputed factual grounds before the accused has had an opportunity to rebut the presumption arising from admitted cheque issuance.
material_facts: The accused admitted issuing the cheques relied on in the cheque-dishonour complaint.
The accused disputed that the cheques represented an enforceable debt and claimed they had been issued to assist with a land purchase.
That defense required evidence, and the accused had not yet rebutted the statutory presumption in the complaint proceedings.
The High Court quashed the complaint because of the dispute concerning the receipts, but the Supreme Court held that the complaint should proceed.
issues.conclusion: The cheque-dishonour complaint should not have been quashed on the basis of the inter-party dispute and unresolved factual questions. The complaint was restored for adjudication after both sides had an opportunity to present evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, admission or proof of cheque issuance raises a rebuttable presumption in favour of the holder. The presumption under Section 139 and Section 118(a) of the Indian Evidence Act continues until the accused adduces evidence to rebut it. Disputed factual questions requiring evidence are not a basis to quash a complaint under Section 138 by exercising power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure; legal issues such as limitation may be considered separately. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_quashed_cheque_complaint and cheque_issuance_admitted and accused_has_not_rebutted_presumption and disputed_facts_require_evidence

predicates.appeal_from_quashed_cheque_complaint: An appeal challenges an order quashing a cheque-dishonour complaint.
predicates.cheque_issuance_admitted: The accused admits having issued the cheque or cheques relied on in the complaint.
predicates.accused_has_not_rebutted_presumption: The accused has disputed that an enforceable debt existed but has not yet adduced evidence to rebut the presumption arising from cheque issuance.
predicates.disputed_facts_require_evidence: The competing accounts depend on disputed facts that require evidence to resolve.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the quashing of a cheque-dishonour complaint, cheque issuance is admitted, the accused has not rebutted the resulting presumption, and disputed facts require evidence, the complaint must be restored for trial.
